author: Om
note: Written by Om without opening the decision trees, with his own answer and reason for each task, before any model run. The runner sends only user_prompt. answer and why are for the person comparing results and are never sent to the model. Text is verbatim from Om's table.

tasks.user_prompt: Ask the user to double confirm they want to delete their workspace and this step is irreversible
tasks.om_why: Deleting the workspace is the primary action being confirmed with a soft destructive button and a secondary button to cancel or icon x button to close the modal to cancel the permanent step in case of misclick or change of heart.

tasks.user_prompt: Present the user with 2 choices, they have to pick one of two
tasks.om_answer: Use radio select, card or radio group
tasks.om_why: It's a clear single select function. When there are only 2 choices, it's a binary choice that doesn't require the additional click of a dropdown to expose options.

tasks.user_prompt: When the user clicks on a table row, they need a way to view all the entry details
tasks.om_answer: Open a sidemanel that flys out from the right side and is inline on desktop and overlays after 800px or less viewport width
tasks.om_why: A side panel that's inline on desktop and overlaps on 800px or less viewport widths allows user ample space to view information in read only state. Dialogs should avoid scroll whenever possible and be used for more ephemeral experiences rather than fixed touchpoints and views that need to be accessible.

tasks.user_prompt: During onboarding allow the user to quickly select all the topics they are interested in
tasks.om_answer: Use chips that can be toggled to selected state with a click. Arrange an array of chips that responsively fit the viewport.
tasks.om_why: It doesn't hide the choices behind a click to expose a dropdown menu. Paired with leading icons, the text in chips reads easily. These are not filters but rather an array of yes/no selections.

tasks.user_prompt: When a section has multiple errors, display clearly to the user what needs to be addressed and the severity
tasks.om_answer: Use an inline alert at the top of the section, below the header to draw attention to the user that several items need addressing. Use helper text below the input, and input state error or notice for respective fields to help users pinpoint and fix each item.
tasks.om_why: The inline alert does the job of calling the user's attention to a specific section of the page. The input state and helper text does the job of calling attention to specific items that need addressing.

tasks.user_prompt: Communicate to the user there is a promotion site wide that's now available
tasks.om_answer: Use a preheader banner sticky to the top with a cta button to take action.
tasks.om_why: Since the information is important enough for all users visiting the site, it's worth putting at the top, making it dismissible but hard to miss at first glance. This can also be used to communicate site wide issues in outages and errors affecting the system.

tasks.user_prompt: Once a user has completed a task or updated a form successfully, communicate to the user the task was completed successfully.
tasks.om_answer: Use a toast in a positive state
tasks.om_why: It's an ephemeral in app notification that gives the user confidence that their action was completed successfully.

tasks.user_prompt: Allow the user to toggle between separate sections of a relation group without incurring page travel
tasks.om_why: They are separate sections of a related group of if a section is integrations and notifications, the notification settings can be a second tab, integrations is the primary default tab.

tasks.user_prompt: Allow the user to input a date either by picking a date or typing it in
tasks.om_why: A specialized input field that allows users to input numeric values in a date format or pick from a calendar menu

tasks.user_prompt: Allow the user to pick a range of min to max values
tasks.om_answer: Use slider with discrete values that allows the user to pick min and max values. Max value cannot be less than min and vice versa
tasks.om_why: It's an error proof format to get values while encouraging the user to understand what their choices are
